title: SecHelix runtime trace v1
description: Runtime observations correlated against static claims. A trace records and correlates; it never generates traffic, and it can never carry a status above HYPOTHESIS, because behaviour observed at runtime is evidence about a claim rather than proof of one.

allOf.description: PRODUCTION_SAFE is never a default. Choosing it requires stating the restrictions under which it was chosen; LOCAL and STAGING need none.

execution_mode.description: Where the observations were collected. LOCAL and STAGING are the defaults; PRODUCTION_SAFE is a deliberate choice that carries its own restrictions.

production_safeguards.description: The restrictions under which PRODUCTION_SAFE was chosen. Required in that mode, because 'we ran it against production' with no stated limits is not a safeguard, it is a hope.

emits_traffic.description: Always false. This contract exists for a recorder; an artifact that claimed traffic had been generated to produce it would be describing a different tool.

counts.description: Per-strength correlation counts. All four are required so a renderer cannot quietly drop INSUFFICIENT and leave a reader counting only what was decided.

notes.description: What would make a reader over-read this trace. Required and non-empty.

redaction.description: What redaction removed, in the shape sechelix_core.proof_bundle records it. A trace that redacted nothing says so; it never omits the field.

signals.description: Observed metadata, one scalar (or array of scalars) per name. Names that would carry a secret rather than describe one are forbidden by the contract, not merely discouraged: a cookie value, an Authorization header, a session identifier and a request body have no metadata reading, so there is no correct way for them to appear here.

kind.description: What was recorded. Every kind is metadata about an exchange, never its content.

surface.description: The route, path or symbol this observation is about. Absent when none was recorded, which makes every correlation for it INSUFFICIENT rather than UNRELATED.

surface_redacted.description: True when redaction altered the surface itself. Such an observation can no longer be compared, so it can only ever produce INSUFFICIENT.

dropped_signals.description: Signal names removed before anything was written, listed so a reader can tell a dropped field from one that was never observed.

allOf.description: INSUFFICIENT and UNRELATED are different answers and the contract keeps them apart. UNRELATED requires a surface that was actually compared and did not match; a surface that could not be compared can only produce INSUFFICIENT; and a match is required before anything may confirm or contradict.

strength.description: CONFIRMS and CONTRADICTS say the observation bore on the claim. UNRELATED says nothing relevant was seen. INSUFFICIENT says it could not be told — which is not the same answer, and is never reported as UNRELATED.

surface_match.description: How precisely the observed surface matched the claim's. FILE means the two agree on a file but not a line, so the match is real but coarse.

uncomparable_signals.description: Signals the claim predicts that could not be checked — never observed, or observed and then redacted. Listed rather than counted as agreement.

allOf.description: A runtime observation alone never makes a claim ready for verification. Readiness requires static evidence, at least one confirming observation, and no contradiction.

status.description: Always HYPOTHESIS. A trace is not a verifier, and a contract that could express any other status here would eventually be asked to.

verification_ready.description: Whether this claim may now be handed to an independent verifier. Readiness is not a status: nothing here has been verified.
